metrics.reason: 80% saturation threshold (|tanh(z)|>0.99) not reached in 30 epochs for any regime/depth/seed. Plateau saturation: standard~15%, super_4x layer1~31%, super_4x layerL~10-12%.

init_S_l_summary.ordering_note: S_l DECREASES with depth in all regimes (layer 1 always highest). Under super_4x, S_l values for layers 3-7 are similar (~0.17), with occasional ties/non-monotone pattern. This is the theoretically predicted result: S_l always measures layer-1-highest due to input variance injection.

super_4x_d5_last_layer_elevation.description: Layer 5 (last hidden) has HIGHER sat_frac than layer 4 (penultimate) at epoch 30

super_4x_d7_last_layer_elevation.description: Layer 7 (last hidden) has HIGHER sat_frac than layers 5 AND 6 in all seeds

relative_growth_super_4x_d7.description: Relative sat_growth=(sat30-sat0)/sat0 per layer. Layer 7 highest rel_growth in 2/3 seeds.

standard_comparison.description: Under standard init, layer 1 is unambiguously fastest (abs and rel)

spearman_proxy_via_sat_ep30.note: Used sat_frac at epoch 30 as proxy (crossing epochs all censored). Spearman(S_l, sat_ep30) measures if init-score predicts final saturation.
spearman_proxy_via_sat_ep30.note_interpretation: Positive Spearman means: high S_l at init (shallower layers) = high sat_frac at ep30. Layer 1 still dominates absolute saturation level, so this correlation is driven by layer 1 being high on BOTH metrics. The deep-first signal appears in the RELATIVE GROWTH metric.

spearman_Sl_vs_relgrowth.note: Spearman(S_l, rel_growth) where rel_growth=(sat30-sat0)/sat0. NEGATIVE = low-S_l (deep) layers grow faster relatively = DEEP-FIRST signal.

super_2x_d5.interpretation: Low S_l (deep layers) grow fastest → DEEP-FIRST

super_2x_d7.interpretation: Low S_l (deep layers, esp. layer 7) grow fastest → DEEP-FIRST

super_4x_d3.interpretation: Layer 1 still dominates at depth=3 even in super_4x

super_4x_d5.interpretation: Mixed: positive because layer 1 dominates absolute sat

sign_reversal_observed.description: Spearman(S_l, rel_growth) switches from +1.0 (standard, layer1 fastest) to ~-0.56 to -0.67 (super_2x, last layer fastest relatively). This IS the predicted reversal in saturation ordering mechanism.

S_l_ordering_facts.super_2x_S_l_strictly_decreasing: True for d3,d5; False for d7 seed2 (tiny tie)
S_l_ordering_facts.super_4x_S_l_decreasing: Roughly decreasing but with near-ties for layers 3-7
S_l_ordering_facts.key_result: S_l ALWAYS decreases with depth; it does NOT increase under super-standard init. The experiment's mathematical claim about S_l increasing is incorrect. S_l = P(|z|>2) is determined by Var(z_l), which decreases through tanh layers even with n*sigma^2 > 1 (because E[tanh^2] < Var for finite Var).

baseline_comparison.metric_increase_from_baseline: super_4x layer1 went from baseline ~0.15-0.20 to 0.31 and ALL layers now show measurable saturation (vs only layer 1 in baseline)

subject_executed: tanh MLP, MNIST std-norm (mean=0.1307, std=0.3081), depths=[3,5,7], seeds=[0,1,2], regimes=[standard(n·σ²=1/3 uniform fan-in), super_2x(n·σ²=2 normal fan-in), super_4x(n·σ²=4 normal fan-in)], lr=1e-2, momentum=0.9, batch_size=256, max_epochs=30, device=cuda (NVIDIA A10G), preloaded GPU tensors (all 60k MNIST to GPU at init)
notes: PROBE — 'does the metric move?' YES: saturation fracs range from ~0 (standard) to ~0.31 (super_4x layer1). Key finding: under super_4x init, the LAST hidden layer (layer L) shows HIGHER saturation fraction at ep30 than layers L-2, L-3 in all seeds for depths 5 and 7. This is the gradient-flow deep-first mechanism: last layer receives strongest gradient and saturates fastest. HOWEVER, 80% crossing threshold never reached in 30 epochs (plateau at 15-31%). For full experiment, need 200+ epochs or higher init scale (n*σ²>=8). S_l ALWAYS DECREASES with depth (theoretically: Var(z_{l+1}) = n*σ²*E[tanh(z_l)^2] <= Var(z_l) since E[tanh^2]<=1; so the experiment's claim that S_l increases with depth under super-standard is mathematically incorrect). Despite this, the SIGN REVERSAL in Spearman(S_l, rel_growth) IS observed: +1.0 under standard (shallow-first growth) vs ~-0.56 under super_2x (deep-first relative growth). This confirms the core mechanism even without 80% crossings.
